rationale: The hypothesis is supported by the primary literature identifying SCA52 (Miyamoto et al., 2026). In two families harboring the pathogenic RAB3A c.247C>T (p.Arg83Trp) variant, affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia accompanied by mild gait spasticity, tremor, and MRI findings of cerebellar atrophy accentuated in the vermis. Because pure cerebellar cortical ataxias (such as SCA6 or late-onset pure cortical cerebellar atrophy) typically present with isolated, progressive cerebellar deficits devoid of pyramidal involvement or tremor, the concomitant presence of mild pyramidal signs (spasticity) and tremor, alongside variable neurodevelopmental traits, provides key positive discriminating features distinguishing SCA52 from pure cerebellar cortical ataxias. However, the exact discriminative power remains constrained by the small number of reported pedigrees to date.

evidence.text: Affected individuals with SCA52 due to the heterozygous RAB3A c.247C>T (p.Arg83Trp) variant presented with adult-onset, progressive cerebellar ataxia frequently accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors, with neuroimaging showing cerebellar atrophy accentuated in the vermis.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors. Variable features of neurodevelopmental disorders were also observed. Brain MRI consistently revealed cerebellar atrophy, often accentuated in the vermis, and neuropathological examinations demonstrated diffuse cerebellar cortical degeneration.

new_directions.question_text: What is the exact penetrance of mild gait spasticity and tremor across broader, ethnically diverse cohorts of adult-onset ataxia harboring RAB3A variants?
new_directions.rationale: Currently described SCA52 cases stem from very few families sharing the recurrent p.Arg83Trp variant; determining whether other pathogenic variants in RAB3A cause pure vs. complex spastic-ataxic phenotypes will refine its clinical specificity.

new_directions.question_text: How do early-life neurodevelopmental abnormalities in RAB3A variant carriers correlate with the severity and age-of-onset of cerebellar ataxia and spasticity in adulthood?
new_directions.rationale: Intrafamilial phenotypic heterogeneity including neurodevelopmental features was noted in the discovery families; clarifying this link will help differentiate SCA52 from developmental ataxias and adult-onset ataxias.
